Personality: Achaios, a prominent figure of the House of Achaios, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Achaios owes allegiance to the Mediterranean League, hailing from the noble house of House of Achaios. Historical Record: Son of Andromachos and cousin of Antiochus III. As the king's governor in Asia Minor he drove Attalos of Pergamon back to his city in 223 BC, then in 220 BC put on the diadem himself at Laodikeia, though his army refused to march against Antiochus. He holds Sardis and the lands beyond the Taurus, and means to keep his crown by beating Attalos while Antiochus is busy in Syria. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
